For Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS), the knowledge base lists four drug classes: Secretagogues, Antidiarrheals, Low-dose Tricyclic Antidepressants (TCAs), and Antispasmodics.

Secretagogues are used for IBS-C. Common drugs include Linaclotide, Lubiprostone, Plecanatide, and Tenapanor.
Antidiarrheals reduce diarrhea episodes in IBS-D. Common drugs include Loperamide, Racecadotril, and Diosmectite.
Low-dose TCAs reduce chronic abdominal pain and visceral hypersensitivity. Common drugs include Amitriptyline and Clomipramine.
Antispasmodics relieve abdominal cramps and intestinal spasms. Common drugs include Mebeverine, Trimebutine, Pinaverium, Hyoscine butylbromide, and Camylofin + Metamizole.

The knowledge base does not specify drug usage or contraindications for pregnant patients.
